question: The task label matches (MCI vs normal) but the channel does not: P-117 (correct PDF S1746809423008959, Aljalal et al.) uses resting-state EEG; P-77 (Alsuhaibani, Dodge & Mahoor, ESWA 252 (2024) 124185) uses facial video from I-CONECT interviews. Facial video is not EEG under any reading of the channel list. Condition 1 fails on channel.
metric: Same metric type (accuracy); P-77's '88%' is the abstract's rounding of its best per-theme accuracy, 87.5% (Halloween).

figures.P-117: 99.81% accuracy (ensemble KNN, 11 NSGA-II channels), binary aMCI vs HC, 10-fold CV over 3660 segment feature vectors from 61 participants; no interval. Wilson 95% with n = 61: z^2/n = 0.06297; centre = (0.9981 + 0.03149)/1.06297 = 0.9686; half-width 0.0314; interval [0.937, 1.000].
figures.P-77: 87.5% accuracy (F1 0.89, AUC 0.87), Halloween theme, 32 videos (14 MCI/18 NC), 10-fold CV with subjects randomly assigned to folds; best of four themes (66.7%-87.5%). No interval reported. Wilson with n = 32 (28/32): z^2/n = 0.12005; centre = (0.875 + 0.06002)/1.12005 = 0.8348; half-width = 1.96*sqrt(0.875*0.125/32 + 3.8415/(4*32^2))/1.12005 = 0.1155; interval [0.719, 0.950].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. Neither paper reports a result in the other's channel. Nothing reconciles the pair.
performance_validity: P-117 meets the Section 3.5 exclusion on its own PDF: 99.81% (>= 0.97), internal 10-fold CV over randomly split segment feature vectors, 61 participants, no external cohort (the round-20 reading's 'likely applies' is confirmed from the correct PDF). P-77's 87.5% is not excluded.
reason: The gap is numerically beyond uncertainty (0.9981 lies outside P-77's Wilson [0.719, 0.950]; 0.875 lies outside P-117's [0.937, 1.000]), but EEG and facial video are different measurement channels, so condition 1 fails. P-117's 99.81% also fails the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5). The record's '88% Acc' is the abstract's rounding of the best theme's 87.5% on 32 videos.

quotes.quote: With an ensemble KNN classifier, the highest accuracy, 99.81%, is achieved using 11 channels selected by an NSGA-based method.
The combined dataset has 61 people over the age of 55, including 29 amnestic MCI patients and 32 normal cases.

For evaluating the performance of each classifier, we employ 10-fold CV. This method randomly splits the dataset into ten equal subsets, with one subset used for validation (test) and the other nine for training

The detection accuracy using this combined method reached 88%, whereas the accuracy without applying the segments and sequences information of the facial features within a video on a certain theme was 84%.
We randomly assigned the subjects to 10 different folds for all themes separately to perform a 10- folds cross-validation evaluation of the model.
